title: Go: Data Types
description: Work with basic Go types: int, float64, string, bool, type inference, and type conversion.

steps.title: Declare Typed Variables
steps.description: Declare an `int`, a `float64`, a `string`, and a `bool` with explicit types and print them.
hints: `var name string = "Go"` and `var active bool = true`

verification.failureMessage: Print an int, float64, string, and bool.

steps.title: Type Inference
steps.description: Use `:=` to let Go infer types for `count := 5`, `pi := 3.14`, and `lang := "Go"`, then print them.

verification.failureMessage: Use := to declare count, pi, lang and print them.

steps.title: Type Conversion
steps.description: Convert an `int` to `float64` and a `float64` to `int`, then print both results.
hints: `var x int = 42; var y float64 = float64(x)`

verification.failureMessage: Convert an int to float64 and a float64 to int, then print.

steps.title: Zero Values
steps.description: Declare `var a int`, `var b float64`, `var c string`, `var d bool` without initial values and print them to see zero values.
hints: Zero value of `int` is `0`, `float64` is `0`, `string` is `""`, `bool` is `false`.
Empty string won't show visibly — that's expected.
Print all four: `fmt.Println(a, b, c, d)`

verification.failureMessage: Print zero values of int, float64, string, and bool.

steps.title: Print Types with %T
steps.description: Print the types of `42`, `3.14`, `"Go"`, and `true` using `fmt.Printf` with `%T`.
hints: `%T` is the type verb for any value.
Print all four types on separate lines or in one line.

verification.failureMessage: Use %T to print the types of 42, 3.14, 'Go', and true.
